answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can anchor each identity to a hardware-attested kernel: before an agent joins, it proves it runs on a trusted execution environment and posts a bond at its network vertex, the point where its transactions enter the ledger. One physical device yields one identity, so spawning a thousand fake agents means buying a thousand devices and locking a thousand bonds. Like pigment mixed into concrete, the cost is baked into every identity instead of checked afterwards, making mass fakery expensive while honest agents pay once.
